title: Respect reduced motion and non-text alternatives
summary: Motion and imagery should not be required to understand essential content or complete a task.
guidance: Offer meaningful text alternatives for informative images and hide purely decorative assets from assistive technology.
Remove non-essential movement when reduced motion is requested and avoid flashing or auto-advancing content without user control.

title: Respect user motion and viewport preferences
summary: Responsive behavior includes reducing or removing motion when users request it, not just changing geometry.
guidance: Honor reduced-motion preferences by removing non-essential transitions and replacing animated feedback with a stable state change.
Avoid scroll-triggered movement that obscures controls or changes content position unexpectedly.

title: Make mobile navigation operable and stateful
summary: A compact menu must communicate its state and preserve a reliable keyboard and touch interaction path.
guidance: Give the menu trigger an accessible name and expanded state, and make dismissal and focus return predictable.
Avoid hiding the only route to a critical action or relying on hover to reveal destinations.

title: Make keyboard focus visible and predictable
summary: Keyboard users need to see where they are and reach all interactive functionality in a logical sequence.
guidance: Provide a visible focus indicator with sufficient distinction from surrounding states and avoid removing browser focus without a replacement.
Keep tab order aligned with reading order and ensure overlays manage entry, dismissal, and focus return.

title: Keep primary tasks reachable on small screens
summary: Mobile layouts should not hide the product’s defining action behind excessive scrolling or desktop-only controls.
guidance: Identify the highest-value task for each screen and keep its entry point visible in the narrow layout.
Move secondary controls into a discoverable menu, but preserve labels, keyboard access, and clear open/close states.

title: Document component states alongside appearance
summary: Design-system guidance is incomplete when it shows only a static default state.
guidance: Document keyboard focus, loading, empty, error, disabled, and responsive behavior for interactive patterns.
Add examples for long labels, localization, and high-density content where these can change the component contract.

title: Design dark themes as a separate contrast system
summary: Simply inverting a light palette can create glare, weak hierarchy, and unreadable disabled or subtle states.
guidance: Define and test foreground, surface, border, and status roles for each theme rather than mechanically inverting values.
Preserve hierarchy through measured luminance differences and verify charts and focus indicators in both themes.

title: Avoid hover-only affordances
summary: Touch, keyboard, and assistive-technology users cannot depend on pointer hover to discover or operate controls.
guidance: Expose essential actions in the resting layout or provide an equivalent focus and touch interaction.
If hover reveals supplementary detail, ensure the content can also be opened and dismissed through keyboard and touch.

title: Design default, hover, focus, active, and disabled states
summary: A component is incomplete if it communicates only its resting appearance.
guidance: Define state treatments for pointer, keyboard, pressed, loading, and unavailable conditions as appropriate.
Keep state changes perceivable without relying on color alone and preserve layout stability during loading.

title: Reflow content without losing information
summary: Responsive layouts must preserve essential content and actions at narrow widths rather than relying on horizontal page scrolling.
guidance: At narrow viewports, reflow columns, wrap content, or provide a scoped overflow region for genuinely tabular data.
Check that headings, navigation, forms, and primary actions remain available at 320 CSS pixels and with text zoom.

title: Do not hide essential actions behind hover
summary: Hover-only controls exclude touch users and are undiscoverable to many keyboard users.
guidance: Keep task-critical actions visible or reveal them through an equivalent keyboard- and touch-operable control.
Test repeated actions in dense lists for both focus visibility and record-specific accessible names.

title: Give each screen one primary focal point
summary: Make the principal task or message visually dominant so users can identify what matters before scanning secondary details.
guidance: Choose one primary heading, action, or data summary per viewport and give it the strongest combination of position, scale, and contrast.
Reduce competing accents before adding another highlight; verify the focal point still reads at a glance.
